data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts using a checklist will be more reliable on average than a single expert using intuition because aggregated independent judgment cancels individual noise, but the single-evaluation signature distinguishing genuine reliability from mere compliance is error decorrelation: genuine reasoning yields errors uncorrelated with the checklist's blind spots, while mere compliance yields errors clustered exactly where the checklist is silent or wrong.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If panel members' errors are correlated (e.g., they share the same checklist blind spot), aggregation fails to cancel noise and the panel offers no reliability advantage over the expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task domain is so holistic that checklist decomposition is infeasible, non-experts cannot apply the checklist meaningfully and the expert's intuition dominates.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the single expert's intuition already internalizes the checklist's verifiable steps, the comparison collapses and the panel adds no marginal reliability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the evaluation only measures final accuracy and not the structure of errors, compliance and genuine reliability are empirically indistinguishable in a single evaluation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Checklist-guided non-experts decompose a judgment into independently checkable sub-questions. When each member applies the checklist independently, their residual errors are largely idiosyncratic and uncorrelated; aggregation cancels this noise (diversity prediction theorem). A single expert's intuition, by contrast, is subject to systematic biases (anchoring, overconfidence) that aggregation cannot remove. Genuine reliability gain is signed by errors that are randomly distributed across cases and unrelated to checklist structure. Mere compliance is signed by errors that cluster at checklist boundaries\u2014cases the checklist did not cover or rules that misfired\u2014producing structured, correlated error patterns.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
